title: How Much Should You Have Saved by the Time You Hit Your 30s
description: Fidelity's '1x Salary' benchmark and how to measure your financial maturity.
content:
Turning 30 is a major psychological and financial milestone. It marks the end of the 'try things out' phase of your 20s and the beginning of the 'wealth accumulation' phase. Financial planners often use this age as a critical checkpoint to see if you are on track for retirement. While every journey is different, data suggests that hitting specific targets by age 30 dramatically increases your probability of becoming a millionaire by age 60. This guide breaks down the '1x Salary' rule and what to do if you are falling short.

Key Takeaways

  • The 1x Rule: By age 30, aim to have 1x your annual salary saved across all accounts (401k, IRA, Cash). If you earn $75,000, you should have $75,000 net worth.
  • The First $100k: Charlie Munger called the first $100,000 the hardest. Hitting this by 30 lets compound interest do the heavy lifting for the next 35 years.
  • Debt-to-Income Shift: By 30, high-interest credit card debt should be eliminated. You should be shifting focus to student loans or mortgage equity.
  • Savings Rate: Your savings rate should graduate from 10% (in your 20s) to 15-20% (in your 30s) as your income likely increases.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The median net worth for Americans under 35 is only ~$39,000 (Fed Data). However, to maintain a middle-class lifestyle in retirement without relying solely on Social Security, aiming for the '1x' benchmark places you in the top tier of savers.

The Benchmark Breakdown

Where should your money be?

1. Retirement Assets (The Growth Engine)

Target: 0.5x to 1x Salary.

Most of your net worth should be in tax-advantaged accounts (401k/Roth IRA). At 30, these should be invested aggressively (90-100% Stocks) because you have 35 years to weather storms.

2. Cash Reserves (The Defense)

Target: 3 Months Expenses.

By 30, the 'Broke Student' lifestyle is over. You need a fully funded emergency fund. You shouldn't rely on parents or credit cards for car repairs anymore.

3. What If I'm Behind?

If you have $0 at 30, you aren't doomed, but you must sprint.
The Catch-Up: You need to save 20% of your income immediately. You can't coast on 10%.
The Lever: Career growth. Income usually jumps in your 30s. Avoid 'Lifestyle Creep' (buying a Tesla) and bank 100% of your raises to close the gap.

Tactical Moves for the 29-Year-Old

  1. Audit the 401(k): If you haven't increased your contribution since you were 22, it's probably stuck at 3%. Log in and bump it to 10-15% today.
  2. Kill the Credit Cards: Enter your 30s with zero consumer debt. Use the 'Avalanche Method' to destroy anything over 7% interest immediately.
  3. House Hacking: If you haven't bought a home yet, consider a duplex. Living in one unit and renting the other can supercharge your net worth catch-up.
  4. Roth Ladder: If you expect your income to soar in your 30s (e.g., Doctor/Lawyer), max out your Roth IRA now while you are still in a lower tax bracket.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does home equity count toward the 1x?

Technically yes for 'Net Worth', but Fidelity's rule refers to invested assets. You can't eat your house in retirement. Aim for 1x in liquid investments.

What if I went to grad school?

You started earning later. Your target might be 0.5x at 30. However, your higher salary should allow you to catch up to 3x by age 40 quickly.

Is cash savings enough?

No. Cash loses to inflation. By 30, you must be an investor. Holding $50k in a checking account is a mistake. Get it into the market.
